## Improved
- **Notifications only when something changed.** The app used to show a summary at every start, and repeat a warning at every check for any mod with open source findings. A Windows notification now appears only when a mod was added or updated, or when a check has a new finding. Restarts and the check every 30 minutes stay quiet if nothing changed. Open findings are still shown in the list.
- **One notification per check.** When several mods change in the same check, they are combined into one notification.
- **Changes stay visible in the tray.** Until you have looked at a change, the tray icon shows a red dot, the tooltip shows how many changes are unread, and the top of the tray menu lists them. Clicking a change opens that mod, and "Mark all as read" clears the list. This also works if Windows "Do not disturb" hid the notification.
- **NEW label in the mod list.** A changed mod has a blue NEW label until you select it.

The first start after updating shows one summary while the app records the current state of your mods. After that, you are only told about changes.

After updating, every mod is compared once more. GitHub's hourly limit can delay some of these comparisons. A finding that a delayed comparison reports for the first time counts as new, so it can give a notification.

## Download and verify
Download `CS2ModVerifier-v0.1.9-win-x64.zip`, extract it, and run `CS2ModVerifier.exe`. To update, exit the running app from the tray menu and replace the old `CS2ModVerifier.exe` with the new one. Your settings and ignored findings are kept.

**Windows SmartScreen will most likely warn you**, because the exe is not code-signed. Check the download first, then choose "More info" and "Run anyway".

This release was built by GitHub Actions from the tagged commit. To check that your download is that build:

```
gh attestation verify CS2ModVerifier.exe --repo KDanielK/CS2ModVerifier
```

Or compare the SHA-256 hash (`Get-FileHash CS2ModVerifier.exe`, or `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt`) with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Please note
CS2 Mod Verifier is an aid, not a guarantee of safety. No findings does not mean a mod is safe, and a finding does not mean a mod is harmful. See the README for what each check does and does not show.
